questions.stem: Why must the calorimeter have a lid during this practical?

options.text: To prevent heat loss so the temperature readings stay reliable
options.explanation: A lid keeps the released heat inside the cup where the thermometer can register it.

options.text: To stop the acid and alkali from reacting
options.explanation: Reacting is the point of the practical; the lid only manages heat.

options.text: To keep the volume of alkali constant
options.explanation: The measuring cylinder controls volume, not the lid.

options.text: To make the reaction finish faster
options.explanation: The lid changes heat flow, not reaction speed.

questions.stem: What happens to the volume of acid added at each repeat of the method?

options.text: It increases by 5 cm3 each time, from 5 cm3 up to 25 cm3
options.explanation: The method repeats steps 1 to 4 with the acid portion growing by 5 cm3 per run.

options.text: It stays fixed while the alkali volume changes
options.explanation: The alkali volume is the fixed one; the acid varies.

options.text: It halves with each repeat
options.explanation: The step is an increase of 5 cm3, not a halving.

options.text: It is chosen at random for each run
options.explanation: The method is systematic, with a fixed step size.

questions.stem: Which temperature is recorded after each acid addition?

options.text: The highest temperature reached by the mixture
options.explanation: The maximum reading captures the full effect of that portion of acid.

options.text: The temperature after exactly one minute
options.explanation: Timing is not the criterion; the peak value is.

options.text: The temperature of the acid before mixing
options.explanation: The starting temperatures matter once; the peak matters every run.

options.text: The room temperature
options.explanation: Room temperature is not the measured quantity.

questions.stem: Which piece of apparatus measures out the sodium hydroxide solution?

options.text: A 25 cm3 measuring cylinder
options.explanation: The method names the measuring cylinder for placing the alkali in the calorimeter.

options.text: A balance
options.explanation: This practical measures volumes, not masses of solution.

options.text: A thermometer
options.explanation: The thermometer reads temperature, not volume.

options.text: A spirit burner
options.explanation: A burner belongs to combustion experiments, not this neutralisation.

questions.stem: The reaction studied here belongs to which family of temperature-change types?

options.text: Neutralisation reactions, which always give energy out
options.explanation: Acid plus alkali is neutralisation, one of the four named change types.

options.text: Displacement reactions, which can run either way
options.explanation: No element displaces another here; acid meets alkali.

options.text: Combustion reactions, which need a fuel and flame
options.explanation: Nothing burns in this practical.

options.text: Salts dissolving in water, which involve no second solution
options.explanation: Two solutions are mixed, so dissolving is not the family.

questions.stem: What goes on the two axes of the graph plotted from this practical?

options.text: Volume of acid against the temperature of the mixture
options.explanation: Those are the two recorded quantities from the results table.

options.text: Time against temperature
options.explanation: Time is not recorded in this practical.

options.text: Volume of acid against volume of alkali
options.explanation: The alkali volume never varies.

options.text: Temperature against the number of stirs
options.explanation: Stirring is technique, not a recorded variable.

questions.stem: Why draw a line of best fit through the plotted points?

options.text: To smooth out reading scatter and reveal the trend in the temperature change
options.explanation: The best-fit line shows the overall pattern despite small errors in individual readings.

options.text: To connect every point exactly
options.explanation: Best-fit lines pass near points, not through all of them.

options.text: To make the graph look full
options.explanation: The line has an analytical purpose, not decoration.

options.text: To convert temperatures to volumes
options.explanation: No conversion happens; the line locates the trend.

questions.stem: The graph shows the biggest temperature change at 20 cm3 of acid. What does that volume mark?

options.text: The mixture that released the greatest amount of energy
options.explanation: The largest temperature difference corresponds to the largest energy change.

options.text: The weakest reaction tested
options.explanation: A big temperature change signals a strong energy release, not weakness.

options.text: The point where the acid ran out
options.explanation: Acid supply is controlled by the experimenter, not by the chemistry.

options.text: The boiling point of the mixture
options.explanation: Boiling is not part of this practical.

questions.stem: How does the conclusion link temperature change to energy?

options.text: A larger temperature difference means more energy was absorbed or released
options.explanation: Temperature change is the proxy for the energy change in this calorimetry study.

options.text: Temperature and energy are unrelated in this experiment
options.explanation: The whole practical rests on that link.

options.text: Energy only appears once the acid is in excess
options.explanation: Every portion releases some energy; the amount varies.

options.text: The link holds only for endothermic reactions
options.explanation: Neutralisation here is exothermic; the link is general.

questions.stem: Which description places this practical in the calorimetry family?

options.text: A reaction in solution is mixed in an insulated container and its temperature change measured
options.explanation: That is exactly the solution calorimetry described for neutralisation.

options.text: A fuel is burned under a copper can of water
options.explanation: That is the combustion variant, not this practical.

options.text: A gas is collected over water to measure volume
options.explanation: Gas collection belongs to rate experiments.

options.text: A salt is heated to drive off its water
options.explanation: That is the dehydration of hydrated salts.
